stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of duodenal ulcers?
rationale: Excessive secretion of gastric acid, associated with Helicobacter pylori infection, can result in the development of gastric and duodenal ulcers.

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of gallstones?
rationale: Small changes in the composition of bile can result in crystallization of cholesterol as gallstones.

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of malabsorption?
rationale: Failure of exocrine pancreatic secretion leads to malabsorption.

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of steatorrhea?
rationale: Failure of exocrine pancreatic secretion leads to steatorrhea.

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of failure of exocrine pancreatic secretion?
rationale: Cystic fibrosis leads to failure of exocrine pancreatic secretion.

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of allergic reactions?
rationale: Celiac disease is an allergic reaction to wheat gluten.

stem: Oligosaccharides are converted into which substance?
rationale: Oligosaccharides are degraded by enzymes at the brush border of the intestinal epithelium to form monosaccharides.

stem: The brush border is part of which structure?
rationale: Oligosaccharides are degraded by enzymes at the brush border of the intestinal epithelium to form monosaccharides.

stem: Monosaccharides are found within which structure?
rationale: Monosaccharides are absorbed by the intestinal epithelia.

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of failure to thrive?
rationale: Lactose intolerance causes failure to thrive when infants are fed on breast milk or normal infant formula.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > DIGESTION & ABSORPTION OF CARBOHYDRATES > Disaccharidases Are Brush Border Enzymes

stem: Lactose is converted into which substance by bacterial fermentation?
rationale: Lactose is a substrate for bacterial fermentation to lactate.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > DIGESTION & ABSORPTION OF CARBOHYDRATES > Disaccharidases Are Brush Border Enzymes

stem: Which substances are transported by SGLT?
rationale: Glucose and galactose are carried by the same transport protein (SGLT 1). Glucose and galactose compete with each other for intestinal absorption.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > DIGESTION & ABSORPTION OF CARBOHYDRATES > There Are Two Separate Mechanisms for the Absorption of Monosaccharides in the Small Intestine

stem: Gastric lipases acts on which substrate?
rationale: Lingual and gastric lipases attack the sn-3 ester bond. The attack by lingual and gastric lipases forms 1,2-diacylglycerols and free fatty acids. Free fatty acids act as emulsifying agents.

stem: Pancreatic lipase acts on which substrate?
rationale: Pancreatic lipase targets the primary ester links at positions 1 and 3 in triacylglycerols. The targeting by pancreatic lipase results in 2-monoacylglycerols and free fatty acids as the major end products. Inhibitors of pancreatic lipase are used to treat severe obesity by inhibiting triacylglycerol hydrolysis.

stem: Which substance is secreted by the liver and emulsifies dietary fat?
rationale: Bile salts are formed in the liver and secreted in the bile. Bile salts emulsify dietary fat into large droplets.

stem: Pancreatic phospholipase A2 acts on which substrate?
rationale: Hydrolysis by pancreatic phospholipase A2 releases fatty acids and lysophosphatidylcholine. Hydrolysis by pancreatic phospholipase A2 allows pancreatic lipase to act on the triglycerides.

stem: Bile salts are found within which structure in the digestive system?
rationale: Bile salts remain in the intestinal lumen. Bile salts are absorbed in the ileum into the enterohepatic circulation.

stem: Which substance is secreted by the ileum and absorbed into the enterohepatic circulation?
rationale: Bile salts are absorbed in the ileum into the enterohepatic circulation.

stem: 2-monoacylglycerols are converted into which substances within the intestinal epithelium?
rationale: Within the intestinal epithelium, 1-monoacylglycerols are hydrolyzed to fatty acids and glycerol.

stem: Glycerol is found within which structure?
rationale: Glycerol released in the intestinal lumen is absorbed into the hepatic portal vein.

stem: Long-chain fatty acids are converted into which substance in the mucosal cells?
rationale: Long-chain fatty acids are esterified to triacylglycerol in the mucosal cells.

stem: Which substance is synthesised by mucosal cells from long-chain fatty acids?
rationale: Long-chain fatty acids are esterified to triacylglycerol in the mucosal cells.

stem: Medium-chain fatty acids are absorbed into which structure?
rationale: Short- and medium-chain fatty acids are mainly absorbed into the hepatic portal vein as free fatty acids.

stem: Cholesterol is absorbed within which structure before being incorporated into chylomicrons?
rationale: Cholesterol is absorbed dissolved in lipid micelles. Cholesterol is mainly esterified in the intestinal mucosa before being incorporated into chylomicrons.

stem: Cholesterol is converted into which substance in the intestinal mucosa?
rationale: Cholesterol is mainly esterified in the intestinal mucosa before being incorporated into chylomicrons.

stem: Which substance is transported by unesterified?
rationale: Unesterified cholesterol is actively transported out of the mucosal cells into the intestinal lumen.

stem: Vitamins are found within which structure?
rationale: Water-soluble vitamins are absorbed from the small intestine either by active transport or by carrier-mediated diffusion.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > DIGESTION & ABSORPTION OF VITAMINS & MINERALS

stem: Minerals are found within which structure?
rationale: Most mineral salts are absorbed from the small intestine either by active transport or by carrier-mediated diffusion.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > DIGESTION & ABSORPTION OF VITAMINS & MINERALS

stem: Calcium absorption requires which substance?
rationale: Calcium absorption is dependent on vitamin D.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > DIGESTION & ABSORPTION OF VITAMINS & MINERALS

stem: Calcium absorption is dependent on which vitamin?
rationale: Vitamin D is required for the intestinal absorption of calcium.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > DIGESTION & ABSORPTION OF VITAMINS & MINERALS > Calcium Absorption Is Dependent on Vitamin D

stem: What is the substrate that phytase acts on?
rationale: Yeast contains an enzyme, phytase, that dephosphorylates phytate, rendering it inactive. High concentrations of fatty acids in the intestinal lumen, because of impaired fat absorption, can also reduce calcium absorption by forming insoluble calcium salts.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > DIGESTION & ABSORPTION OF VITAMINS & MINERALS > Calcium Absorption Is Dependent on Vitamin D

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of intestinal bleeding?
rationale: Intestinal bleeding secondary to malignancy can cause blood loss leading to iron deficiency. Inadequate dietary iron absorption is not the main cause of iron deficiency.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > DIGESTION & ABSORPTION OF VITAMINS & MINERALS > Iron Absorption Is Limited & Strictly Controlled by Hepcidin

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of hemochromatosis?
rationale: Mutations in the hereditary hemochromatosis gene (HFE) regulate hepcidin. Hemochromatosis is more common in the white population of European backgrounds.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > DIGESTION & ABSORPTION OF VITAMINS & MINERALS > Iron Absorption Is Limited & Strictly Controlled by Hepcidin

stem: Which substance is transported by mucosal cells?
rationale: Iron leaves the mucosal cell via the transport protein ferroportin. Iron leaves the mucosal cell only if there is free transferrin in the plasma to bind to.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > DIGESTION & ABSORPTION OF VITAMINS & MINERALS > Iron Absorption Is Limited & Strictly Controlled by Hepcidin

stem: Which of the following is a recognized cause of kwashiorkor?
rationale: Kwashiorkor involves fatty infiltration of the liver. Marasmus is a state of extreme emaciation.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > ENERGY BALANCE: OVER- & UNDERNUTRITION > There Are Two Extreme Forms of Undernutrition

stem: Which substance is synthesized by the liver?
rationale: The liver shows marked augmentation in the synthesis of specific proteins like fibronectin. This protein synthesis is partly driven by the high inflammatory state seen in these diseases.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > ENERGY BALANCE: OVER- & UNDERNUTRITION > Patients With Advanced Disease Are Often Malnourished

stem: What substance is required for threonine excess?
rationale: Excessive utilization of threonine and cysteine in the synthesis of acute-phase proteins leads to catabolism of lean body tissues.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > ENERGY BALANCE: OVER- & UNDERNUTRITION > There Is a Loss of Body Protein in Response to Trauma & Infection

stem: Which substance is synthesized by tyrosine?
rationale: Tyrosine is synthesized from phenylalanine. The dietary intakes of cysteine and tyrosine affect the requirements for methionine and phenylalanine.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > ENERGY BALANCE: OVER- & UNDERNUTRITION > The Requirement Is Not Just for Protein, but for Specific Amino Acids

stem: Which substance is synthesized by alanine?
rationale: Alanine is synthesized by transamination of pyruvate. Aspartate is synthesized by transamination of oxaloacetate.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > ENERGY BALANCE: OVER- & UNDERNUTRITION > The Requirement Is Not Just for Protein, but for Specific Amino Acids

stem: Which substance is synthesized by aspartate?
rationale: Aspartate is synthesized by transamination of oxaloacetate. Glutamate is synthesized by transamination of ketoglutarate.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > ENERGY BALANCE: OVER- & UNDERNUTRITION > The Requirement Is Not Just for Protein, but for Specific Amino Acids

stem: Which substance is synthesised from glutamate?
rationale: Glutamate is synthesized by transamination of ketoglutarate. The remaining amino acids are considered nonessential, but under some circumstances, the requirement may outstrip the capacity for their synthesis.
citation: chapter_43_nutrition_digestion_and_absorption — Overview > ENERGY BALANCE: OVER- & UNDERNUTRITION > The Requirement Is Not Just for Protein, but for Specific Amino Acids

stem: Which of the following is a recognised cause of undernutrition?
rationale: Chronic illness can also lead to undernutrition and protein wasting (cachexia).
